---
title: "Peak Daily Unique Users"
description: "Highest number of unique users on any single day."
---

The highest number of unique users observed on any single day during the
reporting period.

This metric is useful for identifying the maximum daily reach of an application
and for understanding peak demand.

## Calculation

Take the maximum value of `unique_users` over the selected
reporting period, grouped by application.

Group on `application_id`, not `application_name`: a partner can rename an
application, and the ID does not change. Each ID is labelled with its latest name
from
[`events_application_mapping`](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_transformed/events_application_mapping.qmd).
The ID `UNKNOWN` marks events with no application and is left out.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
-- the latest name for each application ID
WITH latest_names AS (
    SELECT application_id, application_name
    FROM   ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_application_mapping
    WHERE  date = (
        SELECT MAX(date)
        FROM   ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_application_mapping
    )
),

ranked AS (
    SELECT
        application_id,
        from_date,
        unique_users,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY application_id
            ORDER BY unique_users DESC, from_date ASC
        ) AS rn
    FROM ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_app_login_counts
    -- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
    WHERE CAST(from_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-05-28'
      AND application_id <> 'UNKNOWN'
    -- to exclude internal CanadaLogin components from adoption reporting, uncomment:
    -- AND application_id NOT IN (
    --     SELECT al.alias
    --     FROM   rp.alias al
    --     JOIN   rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
    --     WHERE  s.is_internal
    -- )
)

SELECT
    r.application_id,
    n.application_name,
    r.from_date,
    r.unique_users AS peak_daily_unique_users
FROM ranked r
LEFT JOIN latest_names n ON r.application_id = n.application_id
WHERE r.rn = 1
ORDER BY peak_daily_unique_users DESC;
```

## R

```r
latest_names <- tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_application_mapping")) |>
  filter(date == max(date, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  select(application_id, application_name)

tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_app_login_counts")) |>
  # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(
    as.Date(from_date) >= as.Date("2026-01-01"),
    as.Date(from_date) <= as.Date("2026-05-28"),
    application_id != "UNKNOWN"
  ) |>
  # to exclude internal CanadaLogin components from adoption reporting, uncomment:
  # anti_join(
  #   tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  #     inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  #     filter(is_internal) |>
  #     select(application_id = alias),
  #   by = "application_id"
  # ) |>
  group_by(application_id) |>
  slice_max(
    unique_users,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # the table also holds the name seen that day; keep only the latest
  select(-application_name) |>
  left_join(latest_names, by = "application_id") |>
  select(
    application_id,
    application_name,
    from_date,
    peak_daily_unique_users = unique_users
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(peak_daily_unique_users))
```

:::

:::


## Interpretation notes

This metric identifies the busiest single day by unique user
reach. The query above also returns the date on which that peak occurred.

## Alternative names

- peak daily users
- highest daily unique users
- maximum daily active users
- busiest day by unique users
- peak daily reach
